findings: Resolved the registered local PDF and verified its SHA-256 and 41-page count against the original audit and manifest. The inspected source identifies Jake A. Soloff, Daniel Xiang and William Fithian, arXiv:2207.07299v2. The arXiv stamp says 21 September 2023 and the title page says 22 September 2023; both are preserved. Equivalence to journal wording is not asserted.

Fresh extraction covers all 25 main-text pages. Independent font-sensitive enumeration finds exactly four CMBX10 Theorem headings: 1 on page 8, 4 on page 10, 5 on page 15 and 6 on page 17. Lemma 2, Remark 3 and Proposition 7 share the numbering but do not enter the Theorem inventory. Figure 8 is the final main-text page. The page-26 heading-only crop confirms Appendix A Proofs; no appendix body was read.

Compared all four original theorem bodies with the rendered PDF. Theorem 5 continues onto page 16 and its saved statement includes all three assumptions, both distributional limits, the extra tail assumption, mean convergence and both variance limits. No theorem transcription correction was needed.

Theorem 1 retains ell<=1 and its exact last-rejection identity, including the nonempty-rejection guard. Only the final max-lfdr conclusion adds the non-increasing alternative-density condition. It does not assume a null-proportion estimator, weighted loss or Chernoff distribution.

Theorem 4 retains fixed lambda in (0,1), the specific plus-one null-proportion estimate, the constrained argmin with weak p_(k)<=lambda, its rejection set and the max-lfdr bound. The previous SL last-minimizer and p_(0)=0 conventions apply. Its equivalence to unconstrained estimated-level SL is conditional on the unconstrained threshold lying below lambda.

Theorem 5 retains pi_0 in (0,1), ell in (0,1/pi_0), the unique interior density crossing, local continuous differentiability and negative derivative, and an arbitrary random tuning variable under its stated convergence condition. Both cube-root constants, both variance constants and the approximate Chernoff variance agree with the source.

Condition (25) in Theorem 5 really prints the negative exponent m^(-1/3) inside its tail probability, unlike the positive exponent in condition (iii). The original statement preserves this difference and the separate source note explains it without repairing the formula.

Theorem 6 retains its own three assumptions, including the one-sided estimator tail condition without an absolute value. The regret constant is the printed power -1/3 of alpha^2 times the absolute density derivative divided by 2 pi_0^2. No two-sided consistency condition is imported from the preceding specialization discussion.

Checked all eleven original source entries and their naming and application contexts on main pages 2-6,10-12 and 15. Model (1), posterior (2), maximum criterion (3), SL rule (4), loss (5), oracle (6)/(7), estimator (12), constrained rule (13), regret (16) and Chernoff variable (22) remain separately identifiable.

The model uses H_i=0 for a true null. Equation (2) defines lfdr as the posterior probability of that event; the abstract reverses the event in its prose. The definition and theorem meanings follow the actual equation, with the abstract discrepancy recorded separately.

The maximum criterion is an expectation with maximum zero for an empty rejection set. The SL procedure chooses the last minimizing index. Chernoff Z is the location of the maximum of standard two-sided Brownian motion minus t squared, not its maximum value. These distinctions agree with the saved source entries.

The weighted classification loss is defined on truth labels and a rejection set without needing a probability model to compute it. Empirical Bayes regret averages the loss difference over both labels and p-values under model (1); it is distinct from substituting a data-dependent threshold into the fixed-threshold population regret formula (17).

Reviewed seven auxiliary passages and nine source-convention notes. They preserve the cost-derived alpha, sorted labels, population threshold, conditional constrained-rule equivalence and exact tuning correspondence. Undefined endpoint ratios, missing random-level positivity conventions, and oracle maximum-attainment qualifications are documented outside the original quotations.

Reviewed the complete local dependency graph: 22 direct theorem uses and 25 deduplicated relationships. D8/D9 are used only by Theorem 4; D6/D7/D10 reach only Theorem 6; D11 reaches Theorems 5 and 6. The proof-analysis Grenander estimator and least concave majorant do not become statement requirements.

Every displayed name retains source natural-language terms. The monotonicity condition is a condition and the constrained rule excerpt is identified by Theorem 4. Highlight selectors correspond to the actual local expressions and every selector occurs in its source entry or a related same-paper theorem. Each relationship explanation follows the reviewed direct use or local dependency.

No content correction was necessary. Archived the previous paper scripts and added an isolated rebuild command using the fixed local PDF resolver. The six JSON artifacts reproduce byte for byte. Reconstruction checks provenance and structure but does not substitute for this manual source review.
